differences.parser: Accepts a literal zero divisor and reports nothing.
differences.reason: The valid corpus fixture evaluates 1/0 and 1.0/0.0 and the real tool accepts it, so the parser must not reject it.

differences.parser: Accepts a real value assigned to an integer target.
differences.reason: No probe establishes that narrowing is rejected; the valid corpus assigns a real expression to an integer target.

differences.parser: Accepts one temporal operand compared with a numeric operand.
differences.sattlint: Requires both comparison operands to be numeric.
differences.reason: Probes accept Elapsed == 5, Elapsed > 2.5 and Stamp == 5; the corpus pins the accepted forms.

differences.parser: Rejects assignment to a plain string target only.
differences.sattlint: Rejects assignment to every string-like target.
differences.reason: The parser accepts Tag = Label for identstring/tagstring pairs; the corpus keeps those assignments clean.

differences.parser: Accepts a DATATYPE with one field.
differences.sattlint: Rejects a DATATYPE with fewer than two fields.
differences.reason: Single-field records are used by the parser's own fixtures and load from disk; the editor UI guard is not a parser rule.

differences.parser: Does not apply the 20-character identifier limit to the header program name.
differences.sattlint: Applies the identifier limit to the header program name.
differences.reason: Corpus program names longer than 20 characters are accepted, so the program name is a label rather than a language identifier.

differences.parser: Emits none of the retired diagnostic codes.
differences.sattlint: Emits some findings the parser retired.
differences.reason: Each retired code was disproved by loading the same source from disk; see RETIRED_CODES.

differences.parser: Accepts a sequence that does not start with exactly one SEQINITSTEP.
differences.sattlint: Requires exactly one SEQINITSTEP at the first position.
differences.reason: The retired-code fixtures load from disk, so the editor UI guard is not a parser rule.
